Amazon will launch more third-party Just Walk Out stores in 2024 than any year prior, more than doubling the number of third-party stores with the technology.

More than 36.7 million items were sold in Amazon Just Walk Out technology enabled stores over the span of a year (June 2024 to May 2025). This combines AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and RFID to deliver a friction free shopping experience, with the aim of saving time for customers and streamlining operations for retailers.

Alongside Amazon, which has 74 Just Walk Out stadium stores and five RFID merchandise stores, the top players include Zippin, a San Francisco-area startup with 85 stadium stores open, and AiFi, also a Bay area startup currently with 26 operating stadium stores that will be joined by 40 or more stores when its stadium-wide deployment at the Intuit Dome in Los Angeles opens later this summer. According to the two Amazon engineers who showed us technology demonstrations, some of the parts of the Just Walk Out technology mix are actually well understood and not extremely difficult to deploy.

claims.notes: Product is widely documented in retail and stadium deployments; while there is public debate regarding the extent of human-in-the-loop assistance, the product itself is clearly not vaporware.

claims.assertion: Just Walk Out by Amazon claims: "Just Walk Out technology uses computer vision, sensor fusion, and deep learning to automatically detect what shoppers take, so there are no cashiers and no checkout lines."
claims.notes: The technology is a well-documented integration of computer vision and sensor fusion, confirmed by industry reporting and technical analysis.

claims.assertion: Just Walk Out by Amazon claims: "Shoppers just grab what they want and go; our AI handles the rest fully automatically."
claims.notes: The claim that it is 'fully automatic' is contested by reports of human-in-the-loop verification, making the 'fully' aspect of the claim unverified.

verdict: The product is a legitimate, large-scale technical deployment. While there is valid public discourse regarding the degree of human intervention versus pure automation, the system is clearly a real, functioning infrastructure product rather than a fabricated or trivial project.

buildability.note: Requires complex physical infrastructure, sensor fusion, and large-scale computer vision deployment, far exceeding a simple software wrapper.
